topic: What frequency planning challenges arise when coordinating multiple ground stations with overlapping satellite visibility windows?
response: Frequency planning challenges arise when coordinating multiple ground stations with overlapping satellite visibility windows due to in-line interference between satellites and terrestrial networks. This includes mitigating interference between non-geostationary (NGSO) and geostationary (GSO) satellites, as well as between NGSO satellites of different constellations. Proper coordination is required to avoid collisions and ensure efficient use of the available spectrum.
reference_context: The reference context discusses various technical challenges in satellite communication systems, including resource management, frequency allocation, and interference mitigation. Specifically, it highlights the need for tight coordination between satellite and terrestrial networks to avoid overlapping frequencies and mitigate in-line interference.
